Using the Beige Book as a cross-check, the tone around late July 2020 is mixed but still negative overall. District reports indicate that activity has picked up from the trough with reopenings—consumer spending improved as nonessential businesses reopened, vehicle sales and manufacturing activity rebounded from very low levels, and housing demand was strong amid lower rates. However, conditions remained well below pre-pandemic levels, with pronounced weakness in the energy sector and commercial real estate, elevated uncertainty about the outlook, and muted price pressures. These Beige Book insights are broadly consistent with the FOMC statement’s emphasis on weak demand, subdued inflation, and considerable downside risks. Combined with SLOOS evidence of broad-based tightening in lending standards and soft loan demand—pointing to headwinds from the bank-lending channel despite improved market functioning—the net tone remains moderately negative, though the Beige Book’s signs of stabilization temper the downside somewhat.
